items.name: Sensitive File Detection — _SENSITIVE_DIRS + _SENSITIVE_PATTERNS
items.description: Two-stage sensitive-file skip: Stage 1 checks parent dirs against a frozenset of known secret dirs (.ssh, .gnupg, .aws, .gcloud, secrets, .secrets, credentials); Stage 2 matches filename via regex patterns with lookarounds (no \b because _ is a word char — 'api_token.txt' would not match with \b). Patterns cover .env, .pem/.key certs, credential/secret/passwd/password/private_key, tokens, id_rsa/id_dsa, .netrc, aws_credentials, gcloud service accounts.
items.counter_case: Cortex already has a security module; adding patterns from graphify's detect.py adds maintenance burden for an evolving pattern set.

items.name: Dedup Variant-Pair Guard — _is_variant_pair + _short_label_blocked
items.description: _is_variant_pair(a, b) — returns True if a/b have same stem but different numeric/alpha suffix (e.g. ASR1603/ASR1605, M1/M1 Pro). Gated by max(len)>=12 check so long labels go through JW normally. _short_label_blocked(a, b, jw_score) — blocks fuzzy merge on short labels UNLESS it's a same-length single-char substitution (DamerauLevenshtein.distance<=1 AND len(a)==len(b)). Prevents false-positive merges that MinHash+JW alone would make on chip SKUs and abbreviation pairs.
items.counter_case: Cortex's knowledge graph may not have many SKU-like entity names; the guard adds code that may never fire in a software-engineering knowledge tool.

items.name: Stat-Based Mtime Fastpath for File Hashing
items.description: Process-lifetime stat index: maps abs_path → {size, mtime_ns, hash}. file_hash() checks size+mtime_ns first — skips full SHA256 read if unchanged (same trade-off as make). Atomic flush via atexit + tempfile + os.replace(). _normalize_path() strips Windows extended-length prefix \\?\. _body_content() strips YAML frontmatter before hashing (so frontmatter-only changes don't invalidate body cache).
items.counter_case: NFS second-resolution mtime creates a 1-second stale window where same-size same-mtime edits pass unchanged; `touch` also causes harmless extra re-hash.

items.name: Dynamic Seed Selection with Score-Gap Threshold
items.description: Selects BFS seeds by stopping when score drops below gap_ratio (0.2) of the top score. When FooBarService scores 1000 and 'error' nodes score 1.0, only FooBarService is seeded (gap 99.9% >> 20%). When multiple identifiers are truly close (both score >20% of top), all get seeded. Prevents high-frequency noise terms from stealing seed slots from a dominant match.
items.counter_case: Hard-coded 0.2 gap_ratio may filter out legitimate secondary seeds when the query has two equally prominent concepts.

items.name: Non-ASCII Query Term Preservation in _query_terms()
items.description: Filters terms by checking `is_english_only = all('a' <= ch <= 'z' for ch in term)`. Drops only English short terms (len<=2) — filters 'of', 'in', 'is' etc. Non-ASCII terms (CJK, Arabic, Cyrillic, Greek) always pass regardless of length. Preserves multilingual identifiers in code search.
items.counter_case: English <=2-char identifiers (Go's 'io', Python's 'os', 'db') may be important search targets and would be dropped.

items.name: _body_content() — YAML Frontmatter Strip Before Hash
items.description: Strips YAML frontmatter (--- ... ---) from Markdown content before hashing. Prevents frontmatter-only edits (date changes, tag updates) from invalidating the body content cache. Applies to .knowledge/ entity pages which typically have YAML headers with updated_at timestamps.
items.counter_case: If frontmatter carries semantically meaningful metadata (entity type changes, status changes), stripping it before hash means those changes don't trigger re-extract.

items.name: Project-Scoped Skill Installs (--project flag)
items.description: Installs skill into `.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md` (project-scoped) instead of `~/.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md` (global). Accepts `--project` flag at CLI. Enables per-repo skill customization without affecting other projects. Useful when Cortex needs project-specific MCP or skill configuration.
items.counter_case: Project-scoped skill files create per-repo maintenance overhead; a global install with project-level config overrides may be cleaner.

items.name: Affected-Nodes BFS + resolve_seed Fuzzy Node Lookup
items.description: resolve_seed(graph, query) tries: (1) exact node ID match, (2) exact label match (case-insensitive), (3) exact source_file match, (4) label-contains match — returns None if ambiguous. affected_nodes(graph, seed, *, relations, depth=2) does BFS over INCOMING edges filtered by DEFAULT_AFFECTED_RELATIONS (11 types: calls, references, imports, imports_from, re_exports, inherits, extends, implements, uses, mixes_in, embeds). Returns AffectedHit(node_id, depth, via_relation) dataclass.
items.counter_case: BFS depth=2 may miss deep transitive impact in highly connected graphs; increasing depth exponentially raises cost.

items.name: Background Git Hook with Rebase/Merge/Cherry-pick Skip
items.description: Post-commit hook launches rebuild as nohup background process (disown), so git commit returns immediately. Skips during rebase-merge, rebase-apply, MERGE_HEAD, CHERRY_PICK_HEAD. Respects Husky's core.hooksPath by reading git config, validating resolved path stays within repo root. Handles linked worktrees via `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` (avoids --path-format=absolute which fails on git < 2.31). Interpreter fallback: reads shebang, allowlist-validates (no shell metacharacters), falls back to python3/python. Marker-based append/remove (preserves existing hook content). GRAPHIFY_REBUILD_TIMEOUT env var (default 600s) + SIGALRM.
items.counter_case: Background rebuild with disown makes it impossible to know if the rebuild succeeded before the next commit; errors are only in ~/.cache/graphify-rebuild.log.

items.name: Code-Only Skip for LLM Semantic Pass
items.symbol: three-pass pipeline architecture: Pass 1 (AST, free) / Pass 2 (video/Whisper, local) / Pass 3 (LLM for docs/papers/images)
items.description: If corpus contains only code files, Pass 3 (LLM semantic extraction) is skipped entirely. Code is handled by tree-sitter AST (free, no API). LLM is reserved for docs, papers, images, transcripts. Aligns with Cortex's LLM-cost-conscious principle — avoids charging tokens for what AST handles deterministically.
items.counter_case: Code-only skip misses architectural comments and docstrings that AST captures structurally but not semantically; LLM-extracted rationale nodes from comments could augment pure AST graphs.

items.name: Community ID Stability via Greedy One-to-One Overlap Matching
items.description: Remaps community IDs to maximize overlap with previous assignment. Algorithm: (1) compute all (overlap, old_cid, new_cid) pairs, (2) sort desc by overlap, (3) greedy one-to-one matching (each old+new ID used at most once), (4) assign fresh IDs to unmatched in size-desc+lexical order. Enables hand-edited .graphify_labels.json labels to persist across rebuilds without drifting to wrong communities.
items.counter_case: Greedy matching may fail when communities split unevenly — a large old community split into two equal halves can only match one, leaving the other with a fresh ID.

items.name: Hub-Exclusion Before Partitioning + Majority-Vote Reattachment
items.description: exclude_hubs_percentile (0-100): nodes whose degree > this percentile are excluded from Leiden partitioning, then reattached by majority-vote neighbour community. Prevents staging/utility super-hubs from pulling unrelated subsystems into the same community and inflating god-node rankings. Reattachment: for each hub, votes by neighbour community → best = largest vote count (min(c) as tiebreak).
items.counter_case: Hub exclusion changes community shapes; downstream tools relying on community membership may behave differently after hub reattachment.

items.name: Cohesion-Based Second-Pass Community Re-split
items.description: After size-based first-pass splitting, runs a second pass on large communities (>=50 nodes) with cohesion_score < 0.05 (actual intra-community edges / maximum possible). Re-splits by running a second Leiden pass on the subgraph. Addresses doc-hub bridges: CLAUDE.md-like files that connect to every node pull distant subsystems into the same community.
items.counter_case: Cohesion threshold 0.05 may over-split legitimate sparse communities (e.g. utility modules with few mutual calls but shared architectural role).

items.name: Semantic Fragment Validation with Hard Size Caps
items.description: Validates untrusted LLM-returned JSON before graph insertion. Checks: fragment is dict, payload <=25 MB, nodes list <=10,000, edges list <=100,000, hyperedges <=10,000 (each <=256 members), node IDs match ^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+$ (max 256 chars), file_type in valid set. Rejects path-traversal via crafted node IDs. Returns list[str] of errors (empty = valid). Called BEFORE sanitize path so malformed agent JSON is rejected before touching the graph.
items.counter_case: Hard caps (10k nodes, 100k edges) may be too low for very large codebases extracted in one LLM call; legitimate fragments from huge files could be rejected.

items.name: Import-Guided Cross-File Symbol Resolution
items.description: Two-level index: global label index (label → node_ids) + Python-specific (module_stem, symbol) → node_ids. parse_python_import_aliases() uses Python AST to parse only top-level `from module import symbol [as alias]` (not nested/function-local imports — wrong scope). find_unique_python_symbol() returns None if >1 candidate (conservative: unresolved is better than wrong). existing_edge_pairs() returns (source, target, relation) triples so a 'contains' edge doesn't suppress a distinct 'calls' edge.
items.counter_case: Python-only module-stem indexing limits cross-language applicability; TypeScript import resolution needs a different approach.

items.name: Global Cross-Project Graph Federation
items.description: ~/.graphify/global-graph.json accumulates graphs from multiple repos. global_add() prefixes node IDs with repo_tag for cross-project isolation, checks source hash to skip re-add, prunes stale nodes for replaced repo. global-manifest.json tracks {repo_tag → {source_path, source_hash, added_at}}. Enables cross-repo queries ('which repos share the UserService concept?').
items.counter_case: A global graph across all repos may become unmanageably large and slow; Cortex's monorepo federation (Phase 11) may be a better fit than a shared file in ~/.graphify.

items.name: INFERRED Confidence Rubric — Discrete 6-Level Score
items.description: INFERRED edges carry a numeric confidence_score on a discrete rubric: 0.95 (explicit cross-file reference, one plausible target), 0.85 (naming + context align), 0.75 (contextual but not explicit), 0.65 (naming similarity only), 0.55 (speculative). EXTRACTED always 1.0. AMBIGUOUS flagged for human review. This discrete rubric enables structured ranking of inferred relationships.
items.counter_case: Adding 6 discrete levels to Cortex's binary EXTRACTED/INFERRED distinction requires updating every synthesis prompt and all consuming code.

items.name: GRAPHIFY_OUT Env Var for Configurable Output Directory
items.description: Accepts relative name ('graphify-out-feature') or absolute path ('/shared/graphify-out'). Used for worktree isolation (each branch gets its own output dir) or shared-output setups. Pattern: `_out = Path(_GRAPHIFY_OUT); base = _out if _out.is_absolute() else root / _out`.
items.counter_case: An env var for output dir location is a footgun — forgetting to set it on a second shell means two processes write to different dirs; explicit --out flag is more discoverable.

items.name: resolve_seed() Fuzzy Node Lookup — closes Flaw #2
items.description: Closes Flaw #2: impact_analysis returns 'Safe to refactor' for non-existent entities. resolve_seed() tries: exact node ID → exact label (case-insensitive) → exact source_file → label-contains (returns None if >1 contains-match, preventing wrong entity selection). Returning None enables proper 'entity not found' error instead of silently treating non-existent entities as safe to refactor.
items.counter_case: Fuzzy label matching may hit the wrong entity on similarly-named symbols in different files; strict exact match + clear error may be safer.

items.name: Edge Confidence Breakdown per Community — partially closes Flaw #43
items.description: Partially closes Flaw #43 (no coverage transparency). Each community wiki article includes an '## Audit Trail' section: EXTRACTED: N (pct%), INFERRED: N (pct%), AMBIGUOUS: N (pct%). Cortex's audit_quality could emit similar per-entity/per-community edge confidence breakdown, surfacing how much of the graph is inference vs verified.
items.counter_case: Flaw #43 is about test coverage, not graph edge confidence; the confidence breakdown addresses graph quality, not software test coverage transparency.

items.name: diagnose_extraction() Edge-Collapse Diagnostics — partially closes Flaw #98
items.description: Partially closes Flaw #98 (no cortex doctor). diagnose_extraction() classifies edges: non_object, missing_endpoint, dangling_endpoint, self_loop, exact_duplicate, directed_same_endpoint_collapsed (pre-build vs post-build edge count loss), relation_variant_groups. scan_producer_suppression_sites() finds seen_* dedup sets in extractor source. format_diagnostic_report() emits human-readable text; format_diagnostic_json() emits machine-readable JSON.
items.counter_case: Edge-collapse diagnostics are specific to the graphify JSON extraction format; Cortex's doctor should focus on knowledge index health (stale entities, orphaned refs) rather than raw edge counts.

items.name: Leiden Community Detection on NetworkX Graph
Honest Benchmarks (worked/ corpus with real inputs + outputs)
IDF-Weighted Scoring with Graph-Object Cache
items.steel_man: Graphify caches IDF on the graph object itself (G.graph['_idf_cache']), which auto-invalidates when the graph reloads — no separate cache key management needed.

items.name: Deterministic Leiden via Sorted Node/Edge Input
items.steel_man: Graphify sorts both nodes (alphabetically) and edges (src, tgt, attrs_json) before passing to Leiden, plus sets random_seed=42 and trials=1 — triple-locking for determinism. Cortex's Phase 14.1 may only set a random seed.

items.name: Video/Audio Transcription with faster-whisper
items.reason: Requires GPU-heavy faster-whisper dep. Violates Cortex's LLM-cost-conscious and no-third-party-API-for-core principles. Phase 0.16 plans this separately.

items.name: Google Workspace Integration (.gdoc, .gsheet, .gslides)
items.reason: Requires authenticated `gws` CLI and server-side Google APIs. Violates Cortex's local-first principle.

items.name: Interactive Graph HTML Visualization (pyvis/graph.html)
items.reason: Python pyvis library generates HTML; Cortex is TypeScript-native. Phase 8 plans visualization in a different stack.

items.name: DeepSeek/Bedrock/Kimi/Gemini/Ollama LLM Backends
items.reason: Cortex has Phase 0.14 for multi-backend LLM. Additional backends are a Phase 0.14+ concern not needing new phases.

items.name: Multigraph Runtime Compatibility Probe
items.reason: Forward-looking infrastructure for MultiDiGraph mode. Cortex doesn't use NetworkX and won't add parallel-edge support in near phases. D bucket until Cortex's graph engine supports multi-edges.

items.name: Anti-Pattern: Bare Filename Stem as Entity/Node ID
items.description: v0.8.13 fix: SQL extractor and Python import resolver used bare filename stems as node ID prefixes — two files named 'models.py' in different directories produced colliding IDs and were silently merged into a single node. Correct format: {parent_dir}_{filename_stem}_{entity}. v0.7.18 further fixed: node ID format should be parent_dir-qualified stems for ALL files.
items.lesson: Cortex entity IDs must be qualified with at least the containing directory to prevent collisions in monorepos with duplicate filenames.

items.name: Anti-Pattern: Partial Manifest Overwrite on Incremental Run
items.description: v0.8.10 fix: save_manifest() was overwriting manifest.json with only the changed-file subset on partial/incremental runs. Next run re-flagged the entire unchanged corpus as new, re-extracting everything. Fix: seed from existing manifest before loop so untouched files are carried forward. Pattern: load_existing(); merge_changed(existing, new_subset); write_all().
items.lesson: Cortex's incremental ingest manifest must always load-merge-write, never overwrite-with-subset.

items.name: Should Cortex use a global cross-project graph index now or wait for Phase 11?
items.question: graphify's global_graph.py ships a ~/.graphify/global-graph.json that federates graphs from multiple repos. Should Cortex add a similar ~/.cortex/global-index.json before Phase 11 (Monorepo Federation) lands?
alternatives: Add a lightweight ~/.cortex/global-index.json now (prefix-namespaced entity IDs, hash-based skip) — enables cross-repo cortex_find immediately at low cost
Wait for Phase 11 which plans proper federation with contract scoring and cross-repo RRF merging
Don't federate at all — Cortex's value is depth-per-repo, not breadth-across-repos
